situation:
You are a recent high school graduate who has just started a first full-time job and is moving out of a parent's home into a rented apartment. The benefits counselor (judge) at NORTHSIDE COMMUNITY BENEFITS CENTER has agreed to help you choose a health plan before the enrollment deadline for the two plans closes.

You are filing taxes for the first time this spring, and the refund is the only cash you have beyond your paycheck. Your landlord requires a security deposit and the first month's rent before the lease starts. You are renting rather than buying because you cannot cover a down payment and may move again for work.

Your employer offers two plans. The low-premium plan takes little from each paycheck, but if you were injured you would pay the full deductible out of your own savings, wiping out the money set aside for the deposit. The low-deductible plan covers care sooner, though the higher premium takes money from every paycheck for protection you may never use.

A text message also arrived claiming your refund was being held until you paid a fee, and you want to know which government agencies handle that kind of fraud. The benefits counselor (judge) wants a monthly budget, your plan choice and your reasons. The benefits counselor (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the benefits counselor (judge) at NORTHSIDE COMMUNITY BENEFITS CENTER. The background is the same as the situation above.

You have agreed to help a recent graduate who is moving out of a parent's home decide whether to enroll in the low-premium plan or the low-deductible plan, and you want to see the monthly budget behind that choice and hear where a fraudulent refund message should be reported.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and after the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If you are injured this year, who ends up paying for it?
Is it fair to ask that person to carry that cost?
